newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND FASTEST IN FIRST DOWNHILL TRAINING RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND FASTEST IN FIRST DOWNHILL TRAINING RUN.

text.p: Downhill ace Luc Alphand saw room for improvement but still managed to post the fastest time in the first training run on Tuesday for Wednesday's race at the World Cup Finals.

"I made lots of mistakes on the bottom, but I have the best time so I must be doing something well," the Frenchman said after posting a time of one minute 39.94 seconds down the 2,704-metre course on Vail Mountain.

A scant one-hundredth of a second slower was Austrian Patrick Ortlieb who squeezed ahead of four other compatriots as the Austrian men gear up to wipe away their disappointment at the world championships in Sestriere.
Two-hundredths of a second behind Ortlieb was Josef Strobl, followed by Hannes Trinkl, Werner Franz and Roland Assinger. Italy's Kristian Ghedina was seventh fastest at 1:40.25.

Alphand has dominated the downhill season with four wins and has easily clinched the season title. But the Frenchman is focused to do well here as he moves closer to becoming the first speed specialist ever to claim the overall World Cup championship.
Alphand holds a 117-point lead over 1994 World Cup champion Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway.
All-rounder Aamodt, who will be competing in all four events here, was 10th fastest in the first downhill training run with a time of 1:40.52.
